Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 91, English)
The Katha of Baba Ramdev Pir (Rama Sarkar): The Kalyug Avatar and Ashaeiynn's Guru Lineage

This session is a full devotional katha (storytelling discourse) on the life of Baba Ramdev Pir (also called Rama Sarkar/Ramsa Pir), deliver ed as part of Mahotsav festivities by a senior teacher speaking on Ashaeiynn's behalf, interwoven with traditional Rajasthani devotional verses (dohas) praising Ramdev Pir . The transcript begins mid-sentence (partway thr ough an intr oductory point) and is almost entir ely a solo narrated discourse with call-and-r esponse chanting, not live audience Q&A — so per the standing template for solo-addr ess content, this is pr esented as a 2-part document (Knowledge Base and Q&A Pairs only), with Part III (Curated Conversational Q&A) omitted.

1. Framing: Ramdev Pir as a Fully Awakened Kalyug Avatar The katha opens by establishing that this divine figure took full avatar (incarnation) specifically within Kalyug, remains spiritually awakened today , and — per his own boon — will remain awakened until the end of Kalyug.

2. Teaching: Why Differ ent Avatars Displayed Differ ent Numbers of Miracles The speaker teaches that Bhagwan Ram, whose divinity was self-evident to all, needed to perform only one or two miracles (such as reviving Ahilya through his touch); Krishna, arriving later , needed to display more miracles to convince people of his divinity; and Rama Sarkar (Ramdev Pir), arriving latest in the most doubt-filled age (Kalyug), needed to display the most miracles of all to establish his identity — described as the historical origin of the "parcha" (proof-miracle) tradition, which the speaker connects to more recent spiritual figures like Bageshwar Dham's Pandokar Sarkar continuing this same tradition of miracle-based "parichay" (introduction/proof).

3. Biographical Basics Per the katha, this figure was born in the year 1401 (V ikram Samvat), lived only 30 years in physical form, and then took jeevit samadhi (a living samadhi, meaning he consciously entered eternal meditation while alive rather than dying conventionally). He was born in Kundu Kashmir village in the Pokhran district of Rajasthan (the same district later known for India's nuclear tests) — an area today home to the pilgrimage site Ramdevra.

4. The Mantra's Origin and Lineage The speaker explains the technical composition of the "Jai Siyaram" mantra used throughout Ashaeiynn: its rishi (sage) is Mata Sita, its beej (seed syllable) is Raam, its shakti is Reem, and its keelak is Kleem. This mantra is described as having been received through the grace of "Parikshit Bhaiya," identified as a realized saint of the category "Brahm Preet" (counted among Hanuman ji Maharaj's principal attendants/ganas), whose own lineage carries an awakened connection to Shri Rama Sarkar across four generations within his family (kul).

5. Teaching: Ashaeiynn's Power Is Rooted in This Lineage The speaker teaches that Ashaeiynn's spiritual power to work with any form of tantra, mantra, yantra, curse (dosh), af fliction, or knowledge of past-present-future flows specifically through Hanuman ji Maharaj's grace, itself made accessible through this same Rama Sarkar lineage — framing Ashaeiynn's practices as fully transparent rather than secretive, centered entirely on the single mantra Jai Siyaram from beginning to end of any ritual.

6. Clarification: Ashaeiynn's Sampradaya (T radition) and Lineage Identity The speaker instructs the sangat that if ever questioned about their spiritual lineage or af filiation, they should identify as "Ram bhakts of the Nath Sampradaya," with Hanuman ji Maharaj as
their guru — of fered so practitioners have a clear , confident answer if their connection to this path is ever doubted or questioned by others.

7. Ajmal ji Maharaj's Twelve Years of Pilgrimage The katha's narrative begins with Ajmal ji Maharaj, a devout local chieftain (seth) in Pokhran district and a devotee of Dwarkadhish (a form of Krishna), who walked on foot to Dwarka, Gujarat every year for twelve consecutive years as an act of devotion, without incident.

8. The Insult That Nearly Ended His Devotion In the thirteenth year , villagers heading to their fields turned back upon seeing Ajmal ji early in the morning, explaining that seeing a "banjh" (childless) man first thing was inauspicious. Deeply hurt, Ajmal ji considered abandoning his devotional practice, but his wife, Rani Sa, persuaded him to make one final pilgrimage.

9. The Bajra Laddus and the Vision at the Temple Carrying of ferings of bajra (millet) laddus to Dwarka, Ajmal ji wept before the temple all day; when a priest asked him to leave for the deity's rest hour , Ajmal ji refused to go without receiving what he came for . In frustration, he threw the (now stone-hard, ghee-set) laddus at the murti; the statue visibly shook. Moved and overwhelmed, Ajmal ji leapt into the sea and, in a state between waking and sleep, received a direct vision of Vishnu reclining on Sheshnag.

10. The Divine Pr omise In this vision, Dwarkadhish tells Ajmal ji that his twelve years of devotion are the very reason he keeps returning, and promises to be born as his son — with the child bearing distinguishing kumkum-colored footprints as proof, and household water turning to milk as confirmation of the promise.

1 1. Ramdev ji's Birth Per the katha, this figure appeared (rather than being conceived and born in the ordinary sense) in a second cradle placed beside that of Ajmal ji's elder son, marked by small kumkum-colored feet — read by the family as the fulfillment of the temple vision.

12. Mena Devi's Early Doubt and Its Resolution Ajmal ji's wife, Mena Devi, initially suspected tantra-mantra/black magic might explain the child's appearance, given that goddess-tantra practices were widespread at the time. Her doubt was resolved when she witnessed a pot of milk lift itself of f the fire unaided — convincing her this was divine, not sorcerous.

13. Selected Childhood Miracle (Par cha): The Flying Wooden Horse As a boy from a royal household, Ramdev ji requested a toy horse; commissioned finely by a tailor , the horse was mounted by the boy , at which point Garuda (V ishnu's divine vehicle) descended and inhabited the toy , causing it to rise into the air . The tailor was wrongly imprisoned and beaten for suspected sorcery until young Ramdev ji himself intervened to clear his name.

14. Selected Childhood Miracle: Redeeming the Demon Bhairav A man-eating figure known as Bhairav (framed in the katha as a person who, having once eaten human flesh, could no longer be reintegrated into society and was ostracized as a "rakshasa") came seeking prey at the monastery (math) where young Ramdev ji was hidden under bedding by his guru, Balnath ji Maharaj, for protection. When Bhairav discovered him, Ramdev ji revealed himself, and rather than killing Bhairav , extracted a vow to stop harming others in exchange for a permanent share of future ritual food of ferings (bhog) — explaining the still-observed practice of of fering Bhairav bhog at midnight during Ramdev ji katha and jagran events today .

15. Selected Youth Miracle: Salt Turned to Sugar A traveling merchant (banjara) named Lakha, attempting to evade a tax on sweet goods by falsely declaring his sugar -crystal (mishri) car go as salt (which was untaxed), was let through by young Ramdev ji, who then miraculously turned the sugar into actual salt as a consequence of the lie. Lakha's remorseful confession and return led Ramdev ji to restore it to sugar , converting Lakha into a lifelong devotee.

16. Selected Miracle: Healing During a Plague (Hejda) During a serious epidemic, mere contact with or the sight of the young prince reportedly healed the af flicted instantly , drawing lar ge crowds; the katha states he revived hundreds of people from death during his lifetime, comparable to Ram reviving Ahilya and Krishna reviving Parikshit.

17. The Five Pirs Fr om Mecca-Medina As Ramdev ji's fame spread even to Mecca and Medina, five of the most powerful Muslim pirs traveled to test him. After he miraculously grew five pipal trees on command, teleported their personal eating bowls from Mecca to
Rajasthan instantly , and produced each pir's specifically requested food, the pirs surrendered fully , declaring him "Peero ke Peer" (Peer of Peers) / Mahapir , and became his disciples.

18. Founding of Runicha (Ramdevra) As crowds grew too lar ge to manage in his existing setup, Ramdev ji founded a settlement named Runicha, which today is known as Ramdevra, still a major pilgrimage site.

19. Selected Miracle: Saving a Mer chant's Sinking Boat A merchant traveling by sea from the west (toward Gujarat's trading community) faced a boat taking on water in a storm; upon calling out to Ramdev ji for help while playing a board game (chaupar), Ramdev ji raised his hand from afar and the boat's water receded, delivering the merchant safely to shore, where he built a temple in gratitude.

20. Selected Miracle: Reviving a Sister -in-Law's Cattle When a sister -in-law (bhaujai) taunted him for merely claiming to be an avatar without proof, after her cattle died, Ramdev ji revived the animals with a glance, and separately blessed her garden/orchard with abundant growth.

21. Selected Miracle: The Contest of Lakes A rival religious figure, Jado ji Maharaj (founder of the Bishnoi community), invited Ramdev ji to test the sweetness of his newly built lake out of pride; upon Ramdev ji's tasting, the lake's water instantly turned salty (khaaro). Humbled, Jado ji apologized, and Ramdev ji subsequently created Ram Sarovar — a lake blessed to never run dry and always remain sweet — which still exists as a pilgrimage site today , alongside Jado ji's original lake.

22. Selected Miracle: The Carpenter (Khati) Friend Revived When a carpenter friend declined to go out and play with Ramdev ji, the friend suddenly died; his grieving family began funeral preparations, but upon Ramdev ji's return and simple call ("Khati, uttho" — "Carpenter , get up"), the friend was instantly revived, cementing devotion to Ramdev ji among the carpenter (khati) community to this day .

23. Marriage to Netal Devi Ramdev ji's bride, Netal Devi (an incarnation of Rukmini, per the katha), had a severe physical disability from birth that was healed the moment she began devoutly remembering Ramdev ji's name after hearing of his miracles — leading her to pray she would marry no one else.

24. The Sister Sugna's Story and Uday Singh's Initial Rejection Ramdev ji's cousin/sister Sugna's husband, Uday Singh, initially refused to allow her to attend the wedding, partly out of prejudice against Ramdev ji's association with lower -caste communities and his adopted foundling sister , Dali Bai (found abandoned in a tree, later revered as an incarnation of Radha). Uday Singh tore up the relationship and imprisoned Ramdev ji's messenger . Only after witnessing repeated miracles — barren land blooming wherever Ramdev ji traveled, cannonballs fired at him turning into flower garlands — did Uday Singh relent, apologize, and send Sugna to the wedding.

25. The Test With a Dead Cat Before the wedding, the bride's mother and sister , wishing to test the groom's divinity , served a dead cat hidden under a covered plate; Ramdev ji revived it with a touch and returned it, convincing the family fully of his divine nature.

26. Post-Marriage Miracles Selected episodes include reviving a nephew (Bhanu) who died of snakebite during the wedding procession itself (called back to life with three calls of his name); correctly telling a pregnant queen that the saint Sadul ji Maharaj was the soul entering her womb; reviving a merchant couple murdered by robbers after visiting him (who then built a still-standing temple); the devotee Harji Bhati's tests by a rival ascetic (producing milk from a never -pregnant goat and water from a dry channel through sincere prayer), after which Harji received trilok darshan (vision of the three worlds) and para gyaan (supreme knowledge); healing a blind, disabled Muslim boy instantly; and punishing then for giving a healer (hakim) who wrongly imprisoned Harji as a fraud.

27. Taking Jeevit Samadhi At age 30, having fulfilled his promise to his father Ajmal ji, Ramdev ji took jeevit samadhi (a consciously chosen, living entry into eternal meditation) on Bhadrapada Shukla Dashami — the same lunar fortnight in which he was born (on Duj, the second day).

28. Dali Bai's Devotion and Parallel Samadhi His devoted foster sister Dali Bai insisted on taking her own samadhi immediately before his and in his place, proving her sincerity by predicting that five sacred items would be found two feet beneath the site if her

devotion was genuine — which proved true upon digging. In response, Ramdev ji granted her a direct vision of his Vishnu form and the boon that her name would always be invoked alongside his, from then on worshipped together .

29. Ramdev ji's Closing Vows Befor e Taking Samadhi At Ram Sarovar , before entering samadhi, Ramdev ji vowed that his samadhi should never be disturbed by anyone; that he would remain more awakened after samadhi than before, present in all eight praharas (time periods) of the day; that sincere remembrance in any form, even in a dream, would cause him to manifest; and that he would remain spiritually awake in this way for as long as the earth exists.

30. Teaching: Dir ect Devotion to Ram vs. Devotion Through This Lineage The speaker teaches that while devotion to Ramdev ji/Rama Sarkar yields the eighteen siddhis and other powerful blessings readily , direct worship of Ram alone (for example, simply visiting Ayodhya) may not yield the same results as readily — framing devotion channeled through this specific guru lineage as the practical pathway through which Ram's power and Hanuman ji Maharaj's grace become accessible to ordinary devotees today .

31. Teaching: Rama Sarkar's Special Relationship to Hanuman ji Maharaj The speaker teaches that Hanuman ji Maharaj, though present everywhere, is described as being especially accessible and somewhat "restrained"/or ganized through his connection to Rama Sarkar , whom the speaker calls the reason Hanuman ji's mantra (otherwise described as fierce/ugra) becomes gentle and immediately gracious when approached via the Jai Siyaram mantra and this lineage.

32. Pr escribed Method of Worship The speaker teaches that the simplest way to honor this lineage is to say: "Hey ji Maharaj, main aaj Parikshit Bhaiya ko saakshi maankar aapke charno mein Jai Siyaram ka jaap kar raha hoon, kripa karke use sweekar karein" (invoking Parikshit Bhaiya as witness while of fering one's Jai Siyaram jaap at the feet of this lineage) — stated as suf ficient to direct the full merit of one's practice to Bhagwan Ram and receive this lineage's grace in return.

33. Closing Blessing The speaker closes the katha by of fering a blessing that anyone who has heard this katha in full — whether live or via recording — will receive Rama Sarkar's swift grace, with those attending live and in person specifically noted as receiving even greater blessing.

34. Closing Logistics: Mahotsav's Havan and Evening Pr ogram The katha closes with practical announcements: a havan would begin roughly 40 minutes later (around 3:15 that afternoon), with an invitation for everyone to participate; an evening bhajan mandali/kirtan program was also planned, described as fully live; and Bhaiya's (Parikshit's) personal attendance at the day's events was left open/uncertain, with the events proceeding as scheduled regardless of whether he could join in person.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This session is a complete devotional katha of Baba Ramdev Pir (Rama Sarkar), a figure the tradition identifies as a fully awakened Kalyug avatar born in 1401 (V ikram Samvat) who took jeevit samadhi at age 30. The Jai Siyaram mantra used throughout Ashaeiynn is described technically (rishi: Sita, beej: Raam, shakti: Reem, keelak: Kleem) and traced through a four -generation family lineage connected to Rama Sarkar , currently carried by Parikshit Bhaiya, identified as a "Brahm Preet" category saint among Hanuman ji Maharaj's principal attendants. If asked about their spiritual lineage, practitioners are told to identify as "Ram bhakts of the Nath Sampradaya," with Hanuman ji Maharaj as guru. The katha narrates Ramdev ji's life from his father Ajmal ji's devotion and the divine promise of his birth, through numerous childhood and adult miracles (parcha) — including redeeming the demon Bhairav rather than killing him (the origin of the midnight Bhairav bhog of fering tradition), converting five powerful Mecca-Medina pirs into disciples, and founding Ramdevra — to his marriage, further miracles, and his jeevit samadhi. His devoted sister Dali Bai took her own samadhi beside his and was granted the boon that her name would always be invoked alongside his. This lineage is taught as the practical channel through which Ram's power and Hanuman ji Maharaj's grace become accessible to devotees, with the simple invocation of Jai Siyaram jaap of fered at this lineage's feet (with Parikshit Bhaiya as witness)

described as suf ficient to receive this grace. This transcript captures a solo katha performance with call-and-response chanting rather than live Q&A, so no Part III (Curated Conversational Q&A) is included in this document. Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 91, English)
The Katha of Baba Ramdev Pir (Rama Sarkar): The Kalyug Avatar and Ashaeiynn's Guru Lineage
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Mahotsav katha (devotional storytelling discourse) on the life of Baba Ramdev Pir , deliver ed by a senior Ashaeiynn teacher .

Q1. Why did differ ent avatars display differ ent numbers of miracles? A: Per this teaching, each avatar's number of displayed miracles ("parcha") corresponds to what was needed for that era and audience — Ram and Krishna performed miracles central to their divine narratives, while Ramdev Pir , as a Kalyug avatar , performed a lar ge, well-documented number of miracles specifically to establish faith in a skeptical age, giving rise to the "parcha" tradition also associated with sites like Bageshwar Dham/Pandokar Sarkar .

Q2. Who was Baba Ramdev Pir , and when did he live? A: Per this teaching, Baba Ramdev Pir (also called Rama Sarkar or Ramsa Pir) was born in 1401 Vikram Samvat in the village of Kundu in Kashmir (Pokhran district, Rajasthan), lived thirty years, and consciously took jeevit samadhi (a living entry into eternal meditation) rather than dying a conventional death.

Q3. What is the technical composition of the Jai Siyaram mantra, and why does it matter to Ashaeiynn? A: Per this teaching, the mantra is structured with rishi Sita, beej Raam, shakti Reem, and keelak Kleem; Ashaeiynn's own use of this mantra is tied directly to this lineage, with Parikshit Bhaiya identified as a "Brahm Preet" category saint carrying this four -generation guru lineage forward.

Q4. If asked, how should an Ashaeiynn practitioner describe their spiritual lineage/sampradaya? A: Per this teaching, practitioners are guided to describe themselves as "Ram bhakts of the Nath Sampradaya," with Hanuman ji Maharaj held as the guru at the root of this identity .

Q5. What led to Ramdev Pir's birth, according to this katha? A: Per this teaching, his father Ajmal ji Maharaj spent twelve years on pilgrimage in devoted worship of Dwarkadhish; after enduring an insulting encounter that nearly ended his faith, he received a climactic vision and a divine promise, which culminated in the miraculous birth of a son bearing kumkum footprints.

Q6. How was Ramdev ji's mother's early doubt about her son r esolved? A: Per this teaching, Mena Devi's initial doubt was resolved when she witnessed a milk pot levitate/behave miraculously in connection with her infant son, convincing her of his divine nature.

Q7. What is the story behind the flying wooden horse? A: Per this teaching, as a child Ramdev ji miraculously animated a wooden toy horse, causing it to fly — one of several childhood "parcha" (miracles) demonstrating his divine nature from an early age.

Q8. What is the origin of the midnight Bhairav bhog tradition still practiced today? A: Per this teaching, Ramdev ji encountered a man-eating figure named Bhairav and, rather than destroying him, redeemed him — granting him a permanent share of ritual food of ferings in exchange for ending his harmful ways, which is the origin of the midnight bhog (food of fering) to Bhairav still practiced in this tradition.

Q9. What miracle involved salt and a dishonest mer chant (banjara)? A: Per this teaching, a banjara named Lakha attempted to deceive Ramdev ji, and in response Ramdev ji turned the merchant's salt into sugar , a miracle that revealed his divine power and corrected the merchant's dishonesty .

Q10. What did Ramdev ji do during a plague outbr eak? A: Per this teaching, Ramdev ji miraculously healed victims during a plague, further establishing his reputation as a divine healer among the local population.

Q1 1. Who wer e the "Five Pirs," and what title did Ramdev ji earn fr om them? A: Per this teaching, five powerful pirs (holy men) traveled from Mecca-Medina to test Ramdev ji, and upon witnessing his spiritual power became his disciples — leading to his title "Peero ke Peer" (Peer of Peers), also rendered as Mahapir .

Q12. What is Runicha, and how is it connected to Ramdev ji? A: Per this teaching, Runicha (later known as the pilgrimage site Ramdevra) is the settlement Ramdev ji founded, which remains a major pilgrimage destination associated with his legacy .

Q13. What miracle involved a mer chant's sinking boat? A: Per this teaching, Ramdev ji miraculously saved a merchant's boat from sinking after the merchant called upon him in a moment of danger , one of several miracles demonstrating his protection of devotees who called on him sincerely .

Q14. What is the story of the "Contest of Lakes"? A: Per this teaching, a rival figure, Jado ji Maharaj, was involved in a contest concerning lakes, which Ramdev ji won, resulting in the creation/establishment of Ram Sarovar as a sacred site tied to this victory .

Q15. Who was Netal Devi, and who was Dali Bai? A: Per this teaching, Netal Devi was Ramdev ji's wife; Dali Bai was an adopted foundling associated with Ramdev ji's household, whose lower social origins became a point of prejudice in the story of his sister Sugna's marriage negotiations.

Q16. What was the initial conflict in Sugna's marriage story , and how was it r esolved? A: Per this teaching, Sugna's prospective husband, Uday Singh, initially rejected the marriage connection due to prejudice tied to Ramdev ji's association with lower castes and his adopted sister Dali Bai; the conflict was resolved after Uday Singh witnessed miracles — including the well-known test in which a dead cat was miraculously revived — that proved Ramdev ji's divinity and overcame his prejudice.

Q17. What miracle did Ramdev ji perform for a queen who was pr egnant? A: Per this teaching, Ramdev ji correctly identified/named which saint's soul was entering a pregnant queen's womb, another demonstration of his spiritual insight recounted in the katha's post-marriage miracle sequence.

Q18. What happened with the devotee Harji Bhati? A: Per this teaching, Harji Bhati, through sincere and persistent prayer , received "trilok darshan" — a vision of the three worlds — granted by Ramdev ji as a reward for his devotion, and Harji Bhati's faith was further tested before this grace was given.

Q19. What other post-marriage miracles ar e recounted in this katha? A: Per this teaching, additional miracles include reviving a nephew (Bhanu) from snakebite, reviving a murdered merchant couple, healing a blind Muslim boy , and an episode involving a hakim (physician) who was first punished and then for given by Ramdev ji.

Q20. What is jeevit samadhi, and how did Ramdev ji take it? A: Per this teaching, jeevit samadhi is a consciously chosen entry into eternal meditation while still living, rather than an ordinary death; Ramdev ji took jeevit samadhi at age thirty after of fering closing vows of eternal wakefulness and responsiveness to those who sincerely remember him.

Q21. What happened to Dali Bai after Ramdev ji took samadhi? A: Per this teaching, Dali Bai, out of deep devotion, took a parallel samadhi of her own, and was granted the boon that her name would always be invoked alongside Ramdev ji's whenever he is remembered or worshipped.

Q22. Does this teaching say devotion to Ram dir ectly is pr eferable to devotion thr ough this lineage? A: Per this teaching, devotion channeled through this specific guru lineage (rooted in Ramdev Pir/Rama Sarkar) is taught to yield spiritual siddhis (attainments) more
readily than direct, unmediated worship of Ram alone.

Q23. What is Rama Sarkar's special r elationship to Hanuman ji Maharaj? A: Per this teaching, Rama Sarkar (Ramdev Pir) is understood to hold a special, closely bound relationship to Hanuman ji Maharaj within this lineage's spiritual framework, reinforcing Hanuman ji's role as the guru at the root of the tradition.

Q24. What is the pr escribed method of worship taught in this session? A: Per this teaching, the prescribed method is simple: practitioners are guided to invoke Parikshit Bhaiya as witness while of fering Jai Siyaram jaap "at this lineage's feet," rather than requiring elaborate ritual.

Q25. Was this katha deliver ed by Parikshit Bhaiya personally? A: Not necessarily — per this transcript, the katha was delivered by a senior Ashaeiynn teacher speaking on the lineage's behalf during Mahotsav festivities; the speaker references "hamare Bhaiya" separately and expresses uncertainty about whether Bhaiya himself would be attending live.

Q26. What closing logistics wer e announced at the end of this session? A: Per this teaching's closing remarks, attendees were informed about Mahotsav's ongoing havan and the evening program to follow , alongside a closing blessing extended to all present.

Q27. Does this transcript include live audience Q&A? A: No — per the standing template for this kind of content, this transcript is almost entirely a solo narrated katha performance with call-and-response chanting, not live audience interaction, so this session is documented as a 2-part deliverable (Knowledge Base and Q&A Pairs only), with no Curated Conversational Q&A section.
Bot Response Guidelines

Present this katha's miracle stories (flying horse, Bhairav redemption, salt-to-sugar , plague healing, boat rescue, lake contest, dead-cat revival, and others) as traditional devotional narrative content from this specific katha performance, not as claims requiring independent verification. When explaining Ashaeiynn's guru lineage or the Jai Siyaram mantra's origin, ground answers in this session's specific framing (Ramdev Pir/Rama Sarkar lineage, Nath Sampradaya identity , Hanuman ji Maharaj as guru) rather than generic Hindu tradition. Note, if relevant, that this katha was delivered by a senior teacher on Ashaeiynn's behalf during Mahotsav , not necessarily by Parikshit Bhaiya personally .
